clue.text: Blush over a right-winger being deliberately offensive

indicators.note: over in a down-the-page or turned-over sense tells us to read the blushing phrase backwards

parts.note: to blush is to go red
a Tory is a right-wing Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone colours up after a Conservative politician makes a remark meant to wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works as a reversal signal here: the two-word phrase for blushing is read backwards before the article and the Conservative are attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that belittle or disparage are hurtful on purpose, which is what deliberately offensive describes.

clue.text: Clean frock

definitions.meaning: to clean and bandage a wound, or prepare a bird for cooking
a frock is a woman's garment, a gown

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: preparing a wound or carcass for use, and a one-piece garment worn by women.

clue.text: Destruction, dreadful out in Iran

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the following words are in a terrible state, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A report of terrible destruction somewhere out in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin and wreckage brought about completely is a synonym for destruction.

clue.text: It's wrong to charge bloke stealing one vegetable

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so the letter for one goes inside the jumble
it's wrong says the following letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A moral claim that it is unjust to accuse a man of pinching a single vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's wrong' rearranges TO CHARGE BLOKE; 'stealing' takes I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible thistle head, eaten for its fleshy bracts, is a garden vegetable.

clue.text: Article on more complex proposition that has been proved

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar

indicators.note: complex means intricately tangled, so the word more is rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar point about an article, followed by a complicated mathematical statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' is the anagram signal, not part of the definition; 'on' simply joins the article to the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a statement established by logical proof from axioms is exactly this kind of result.

clue.text: A large number, nearly all in administration

indicators.note: nearly all says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a regiment can mean a large array or number of things

explanation.surface: A comment that nearly everyone employed works in administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' drops the final T from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic sense of the word is government or rule, a system of administration, as well as a prescribed diet.

clue.text: Dramatist's adage about husband

definitions.note: read as Dramatist is, the 's linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the saying goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or adage

explanation.surface: A playwright's favourite proverb concerns married men.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw, Irish author of Pygmalion and Saint Joan, was a celebrated playwright.

clue.text: Difficult getting round in store

indicators.note: in says the round letter goes inside the word for difficult

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is round in shape, so it stands for round

explanation.surface: Something tricky about getting around inside a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'in' places O inside HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile or cache kept hidden away is a store, as noun or verb.

clue.text: "Battle'" almost describes potty game

indicators.note: describes in its sense of tracing round, so the shortened battle encloses the potty
almost means the final letter of the battle's name is lost

parts.note: Waterloo is the 1815 battle where Napoleon was defeated
a po is a chamber pot, a potty

explanation.surface: A quoted word, 'Battle', almost sums up a ridiculous sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the battle's last letter; 'describes' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round, so the shortened battle encloses the potty.
explanation.definitionFit: A team ball sport played in a swimming pool is a game.

clue.text: In this one's after a mate, though there are no men to be seen

definitions.text: In this one's after a mate, though there are no men to be seen

parts.words: In this one's after a mate, though there are no men to be seen
parts.note: a player aims for checkmate while playing without sight of the board or its pieces

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone looking for a partner where no men are around.
explanation.walkthrough: Mate means checkmate and men are chess pieces; in this game players keep the position in their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: In this form of the board game, the players cannot see the board, calling moves from memory.

clue.text: Perfect example in beginning of early religious book

indicators.note: beginning of takes only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, religious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: An early religious text is held up as the model of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that embodies a quality in its purest form is its quintessence, the perfect example.

clue.text: Brave face social worker put on

parts.note: face as in nerve or cheek, which is gall
an ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A care worker puts on a courageous expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a council employee but an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A courageous, spirited person is described as gallant, a synonym for brave.

clue.text: Caught with peculiar instrument

parts.note: snared means caught in a trap
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone was caught carrying a strange musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum with wires stretched across its lower head is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Floor of drain in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bottom of a broken drain pipe needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, its bottom level, is its floor in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Willow — exceptionally large one seen approaching centre of Limerick

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for very large
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letters of the eight-letter word that follows

explanation.surface: A huge willow tree is seen near the middle of the Irish city of Limerick.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Band of gold artist put round part of the trunk

indicators.note: put round means the gold-and-artist letters wrap around the body part

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the chest is part of the torso, or trunk

explanation.surface: A gold ring by an artist placed around part of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put round' has the gold and artist pieces flank the body part; 'trunk' means the human torso, not a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of musicians playing together is a band.

clue.text: Aims often set out in this

definitions.text: Aims often set out in this

indicators.note: set out means arranged differently, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party's goals are usually laid out in this document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges AIMS OFTEN; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A published declaration of a party's policies and intentions is where its aims are laid out.

clue.text: Drink associated with old Victorian tramp?

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic drink taken at the end of the day, around sunset
in old Australian usage a vagrant who turned up at a station at sunset for food and lodging; Victoria is an Australian state

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an evening tipple and a swagman arriving at dusk to avoid work.

clue.text: Informal note about a runner

parts.note: candid, as in an unposed, informal photograph
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A casual memo concerning someone running in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' merely sits between the pieces, joining the note to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for election is said to run, so a contender is a runner.

clue.text: One in a tub, or one in a crate?

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside a and the word for tub

parts.note: a vat is a large tub
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A riddle comparing someone sitting in a bathtub with someone in a packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: Crate is slang for an old rickety aeroplane, so one in a crate is a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is old slang for an aeroplane, so whoever flies one is a pilot.

clue.text: Caustic lime ultimately found on rat, for example

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word before

parts.note: a rat is an example of a rodent

explanation.surface: Corrosive lime has been found on a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that corrodes or eats away, like an acid, is caustic.

clue.text: Slow or fast time set by leader in Olympics.

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: leader in takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Whether the pace is slow or fast, a time is set by the Olympic front-runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word; 'fast' means abstinence, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning to be played at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Soil shortage duke ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the duke's letter is left out

parts.note: a dearth is a scarcity or shortage

explanation.surface: A nobleman pays no attention to a lack of soil on his estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground or dirt that plants grow in is soil.

clue.text: Breed fish, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the fish's name is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: rays are flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: An instruction to farm fish, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear or bring up animals is to breed them.

clue.text: Annoyed after golf club medal

indicators.note: after places the annoyed word behind the golf club

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated after a golf club awards a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A German military decoration for bravery, so a medal.

clue.text: Auction, first of many in state capital

parts.note: an auction is a sale

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An auction, the first of many, held in a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the US state of Oregon.

clue.text: Pass across entrance to hilly copse

indicators.note: across means the pass stretches over and around the letter

parts.note: a ticket is a pass for admission

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A path leads across the way into a hillside wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense group of bushes or small trees is a copse.

clue.text: Unknown number fired from outside, non-stop

indicators.note: fired from means dismissed, so the unknown is removed from the word

parts.note: external means outside
x is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Some mystery figure was shot from outside, and it went on without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting forever without end is going on continuously, without stopping.

clue.text: Top copy plus ten

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A sum: the best copy plus ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or tip of something is its top.

clue.text: Drug supplied by Trust — rheum treated

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A health trust supplies a medicine for a streaming cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Rheum is watery discharge from the nose or eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug given to make someone speak freely and honestly under questioning.
